title: Efficiency of Sequential Negative-Control Survival Adjustment under Censoring
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; projected paper-score ceiling 6.6 < 7.4 and not salvageable within scope. Math-referee-passed, but not decision-clean, novelty-cleared, or D0.5-accepted.
gap_reasons: The attainment proof derives its nuisance and numerical controls, but delivers pointwise inference on known positive mixed-support charts with s>2, leaving weaker-positivity and changing-support inference unsettled.

The reproduced 2.56857% efficiency gain concerns an always-observed primary outcome with early-or-terminal N censoring, and its neighborhood preserves those supports; it supplies no quantitative account of gains across general jointly censored designs.

Exhaustive sieve enumeration establishes computability, while the absence of an implemented estimator or finite-sample evaluation limits the package's practical significance and projected journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the common-N coupled canonical gradient, comparator frontier, continuous strict-gain witness, primitive attainment and Ashby-model transfer; the math referee passed the note and all five classical leaves were source-attested. D0.5 stopped below the field floor at subfield tier, with paper-score ceiling 6.6 < 7.4 and no bounded same-scope improvement. Comparator and citation-positioning findings remain; no formalization or Lean verification was attempted, and field-tier pursuit requires a materially stronger re-anchor.
tldr: The literal sequential survival adjustment of Ashby et al. can be undefined under their written landmark positivity, and can be valid without being efficient. The completed continuous witness audit gives sequential variance \(0.45213232601285\) versus canonical variance \(0.44051897392739\), an exact gap of \(56687107059/4881201107300\), or \(2.56857\) percent of the sequential variance. The accepted source-model transfer checks the published potential-outcome hypotheses and the relevant tangent closure; inclusion alone is not used to equate bounds. The coupled common-negative-control system supplies the canonical gradient for unknown dependent separate clocks and common clocks. Primitive literal-domain, validity and zero-gain tests separate the comparison regimes, and a sample-only event-fit/independent-Gram estimator attains the bound on the maintained smooth and finite subclasses. Undefined and invalid comparators receive no variance ranking.
gap: The same primary-survival target has a sequential adjustment in Ashby et al. \cite{AshbyEtAl2026}, but selecting a full-data efficient function does not solve restricted observed efficiency. Bivariate inversion and generic restricted-gradient characterization are already occupied. The missing result is the explicit common-negative-control cross-arm system, literal comparator frontier and feasible continuous attainment.
fill: Theorems \(\text{thm:coupled-canonical-gradient}\), \(\text{thm:primitive-validity}\), and \(\text{thm:primitive-efficiency-frontier}\) bind the coupled gradient and checkable frontier. The construction question and \(\text{thm:efficient-attainment}\) bind a feasible estimator and fixed-time inference from the supplied primitive charts. No generic projection or finite Fisher calculation is counted as the field contribution. Proposition \(\text{prop:source-positivity-map}\) relates the published truncated endpoint positivity to the formal source clauses, and Proposition \(\text{prop:witness-domain-audit}\) verifies the continuous strict-gain member clause by clause.
